title: Documents into answers.
name: AI Document Search (RAG Chatbot)
description: Chat with PDFs using semantic retrieval and answers grounded in source passages.
detail: PDF ingestion, semantic search, and retrieval-augmented answers in a React workspace. Python FastAPI backend, LangChain, OpenAI, and a local FAISS index.

evidence.imageAlt: AI Document Search local workspace with a PDF library and document chat.
evidence.caption: Actual local application: PDF library and document-chat workspace.
evidence.result: A live OpenAI check indexed the fictional Atlas PDF and answered its budget question with “$4,800” plus a supporting passage from page 2.
evidence.method: PDF ingestion → passage chunking → FAISS retrieval → source-grounded generation. Python tests use deterministic doubles, including a mocked wire-level API contract.
evidence.limit: This verifies one synthetic-document integration path. It is not a retrieval-accuracy or latency benchmark.

imageAlt: AI Document Search local workspace with a PDF library and document chat.

title: A second pair of eyes.
name: AI Code Review Bot
description: Automatic GitHub PR feedback with validated inline findings and human review.
detail: Reviews pull-request diffs and validates findings against added lines before posting advisory comments. Includes a local review workspace, SQLite history, signed webhooks, and a trusted GitHub Actions workflow. Never executes reviewed code or approves merges.

evidence.imageAlt: AI Code Review Bot showing a synthetic payment diff and two validated findings.
evidence.caption: Actual live-model output on a synthetic diff: SQL injection and division by zero.
evidence.result: A live model review identified SQL injection and division by zero in a synthetic payment diff. A separate GitHub Actions smoke test posted an inline division-by-zero comment on PR #1.
evidence.method: Parse the diff, request a structured review, validate findings against added lines, then publish an advisory COMMENT review against the expected commit. The test PR was closed without merging.
evidence.limit: Seeded examples demonstrate integration behavior, not general defect-detection precision or recall. Reviewed code is never executed, and the bot does not approve merges.

imageAlt: AI Code Review Bot showing a synthetic payment diff and two validated findings.

title: An assistant that remembers.
name: Custom AI Agent With Memory
description: A voice and text assistant that recalls only the details you choose to save.
detail: Explicit long-term memory with semantic retrieval, editable Whisper transcripts, visible context sources, and memory deletion/export controls. Local ChromaDB persistence and a Streamlit workspace; no autonomous external actions.

evidence.imageAlt: Custom AI Agent With Memory showing a real local conversation and memory controls.
evidence.caption: Actual local workspace: chat, voice-note input, and explicit memory controls.
evidence.result: A synthetic project detail was embedded, saved in ChromaDB, recalled after reopening the store, used in a fresh conversation, and deleted successfully. A live Whisper request also transcribed synthetic speech.
evidence.method: Explicit save → OpenAI embeddings → local ChromaDB → bounded LangChain context. Automated checks cover persistence, duplication, relevance filtering, deletion, memory opt-out, and audio validation.
evidence.limit: These are workflow checks, not a memory-accuracy benchmark. The app is local and single-user; conversations are session-only while selected memories persist.

imageAlt: Custom AI Agent With Memory showing a real local conversation and memory controls.

title: Making value measurable.
name: Permit Valuation Assistant
description: Saved-model permit estimates from a 5,000-row sample, with validated inputs and documented evaluation.
detail: Training-only preprocessing and a saved regression pipeline produce every valuation. Capped-target evaluation is documented; optional factor explanations cannot change the model output.

evidence.imageAlt: Permit Valuation Assistant showing validated form inputs and a model-predicted valuation.
evidence.caption: Actual local model output for one example input. The displayed estimate is not a measured accuracy score.
evidence.result: On a 5,000-record sample, the saved regression pipeline achieved holdout R² 0.7803 and log RMSE 2.2335. Dollar MAE was $178,907 and dollar RMSE $829,198 against the capped target.
evidence.method: 3,500 training / 1,500 test records with seed 42. Fit preprocessing and the 99th-percentile target cap on training data only; evaluate log1p of capped valuation on the untouched random holdout.
evidence.limit: Log-scale R² is not dollar accuracy. Dollar errors are large, the target is capped, and the sample has limited category/date/location variety. This does not establish future appraisal performance.

imageAlt: Permit Valuation Assistant showing validated form inputs and a model-predicted valuation.

title: Better signals. Better predictions.
name: Heart Attack Classification
description: Leakage-controlled comparison of classifiers on a supplied health-survey sample.
detail: Corrected logistic baseline: ROC-AUC 0.8004 and average precision 0.2040. At the default threshold it predicts no positive cases; oversampling trades more recall for false positives. Three-fold training CV and an untouched test split are documented. Retrospective self-reported history, not future clinical risk.

name: Maternal Birthweight Analysis
title: Birth-weight patterns, carefully examined.
description: Report-aligned analysis of 1,236 birth records using imputation, EDA, t-tests, chi-square, and ANOVA.
detail: Reconstructed SAS source reproduces the report’s headline statistics in independent checks: one-sample p=0.002416, smoking-group Welch t=8.6398, smoking–parity p=0.753378, and age-group ANOVA p=0.538677. Collaborative work with Devadharshini Udayakumar and Prithwiraj Chatterjee. SAS execution is pending. Observational associations do not establish causation.
imageAlt: Maternal Birthweight Analysis — independently calculated result figure

name: Sleep Treatment Response
title: Measuring a paired response.
description: Paired inference and planning curves for drug and placebo sleep measurements in 10 participants.
detail: Mean paired increase: 1.72 hours; 95% CI 0.481–2.959; two-sided p=0.01192. Includes normality checks, a placebo benchmark comparison, and a corrected power-planning model. Results independently checked; SAS execution pending.
imageAlt: Sleep Treatment Response — independently calculated result figure

name: Melanoma Lifetime Comparison
title: Comparing observed lifetimes.
description: Mean observed-time comparison across two nodule-severity groups, with explicit censoring limitations.
detail: 417 observations grouped as nodule categories 1–2 versus 3–4. One-sided Welch t=3.4955, p=0.0002693. The original analysis assumes observed times are true lifetimes and ignores censoring; this is not a censoring-aware survival analysis. SAS execution pending.
imageAlt: Melanoma Lifetime Comparison — independently calculated result figure

name: Survey Response Association
title: From counts to association.
description: Contingency tables and relative-risk estimation for 27,802 aggregate survey responses.
detail: Uses expected-count diagnostics, Pearson chi-square, conditional proportions, and explicitly ordered relative risk. Female/Male affirmative-response RR=2.7556 (95% CI 2.6695–2.8445). Association is not causation. SAS execution pending.
imageAlt: Survey Response Association — independently calculated result figure

name: Ratings Distribution Analysis
title: Understanding categorical patterns.
description: Marginal, joint, and conditional rating distributions from 18 supplied observations.
detail: Correctly oriented conditional tables estimate ratings within recorded gender categories. Personal names and row identifiers are omitted. Small-sample descriptive analysis with independently checked counts; SAS execution pending.
imageAlt: Ratings Distribution Analysis — independently calculated result figure

name: Tuition Trend Analysis
title: Tracing tuition over time.
description: SAS workflow for tuition distributions, five-number summaries, regression, and residual diagnostics.
detail: Source recovered from the supplied code PDF. The original university tuition dataset is unavailable, so no coefficients or numerical results are claimed. Repository includes the expected schema and steps to run once the input is recovered.

name: Fluoride Treatment Effects
title: Separating treatment and context.
description: Factorial ANOVA workflow for treatment, institution, and changes in DMFT.
detail: SAS GLM analysis includes treatment-by-institution interaction, additive and treatment-only comparisons, adjusted post-hoc tests, and residual diagnostics. The original dataset is unavailable; no numerical findings are claimed.
